summary: The triangle-cap implication correctly handles every sign, repetition, and equality case and yields the strict centroid-coordinate contrapositive. The accepted cross-cap bounds, reconstruction theorem, and three-eighths exclusion are applied within their stated surviving-model scope; all strict inequalities are preserved. The centroid midpoint is compatible, has the asserted negative first two coordinates, and its slice-plane coordinate sum forces the third coordinate to exceed one. The conclusion and chamber exclusion exactly match the proved scope, while the proper-cap hypothesis is harmlessly retained although the argument proves a stronger statement.
